1. On the Layout tab, click the Formula command.

3. Type the variables and set the equations in the Formula box.
4. To finish, press Alt + Enter to insert the equation in your document.

To add a footnote in a Microsoft Word document, click the "Review" tab in the top menu bar. Then, click the "Comments" option, followed by "Insert Footnote". A new box will appear at the top of the page, where you can type the footnote. After typing the footnote, click "Save" and it will appear as a subscripted letter in the text.

This infographic summarizes the legal proceedings surrounding Microsoft's antitrust lawsuit. In 1992, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Microsoft alleging that the company had abused its monopoly in the mobile phone market. The case included numerous appeals to various courts, resulting in Microsoft being found innocent and never required to change its business practices. In 2005, Microsoft and the Justice Department reached a settlement, with Microsoft being ordered to pay US$75 billion in fines. This antitrust lawsuit has had little impact on the software industry, as large technology companies continue to face no scrutiny for their business practices.

Microsoft Word and Google Docs are both word processing programs used to create documents. Google Docs is a traditional software program that comes on the Windows operating system and must be purchased for use. Microsoft Word is a cloud-based application that is offered for free as part of the Google suite. Microsoft Word offers more direct control over page formatting and design, while Google Docs offers real-time collaboration and cloud storage. Both programs offer robust features including tables, images, formatting, and more.

Microsoft Office offers fewer advanced features, lacking macros and VBA scripting, and has limited formatting and graphic options. Google Docs, on the other hand, has a more complex user experience focused on offline editing, making it harder to share and collaborate with others. It also has a more extensive feature set than Microsoft Office.

Microsoft Excel is word processing software that allows users to write, format, and print documents. It facilitates document editing by allowing users to perform functions such as spell-checking and mail merging. Excel also provides tools for drawing and enables users to create interactive presentations with live data. With its flexible user interface, Microsoft Excel makes it easy to create and print documents quickly and accurately.

Microsoft Access is a spreadsheet program, while Microsoft Excel is a database management program. Excel is better suited for storing and managing large amounts of data, while Access is better suited for creating spreadsheets and performing calculations. Excel utilizes powerful query tools that enable users to search and manipulate large datasets, while Access focuses more on creating and formatting documents with charts and charts. In addition, Excel is better for creating complex data entry forms, while Access is better for creating complex formulas and calculations.

To create a checklist in Microsoft Word, open a new Word document. Click the Insert tab, then choose the Chart option. Select a 2-column table and add your checklist items. Type a hyphen (-) or an "X" in the left column to indicate an unchecked item. Click the Review tab, then select the Bullets option and choose the checkmark icon to insert a checked item. You can also select the desired font and font size from the Home tab.
